claim: A check whose process was killed apart answers `died on SIGKILL apart, so it judged nothing —` with an empty error stream, and nothing there or anywhere on disk says which sender signalled it. Three leave the same words: the check's own audit processor ceiling, which a watcher enforces by writing `cgroup.kill`; the sweep of groups a run left behind, which writes `cgroup.kill` to any group whose maker looks gone and runs on every spawn and every reaper tick; and a kill from outside. Only the memory reaper can be ruled out from a log, since it signals SIGTERM first and names what it took. The round that would settle it records no cost, because a check's cost is written by the child that died. So a killed check under memory pressure reads as the reaper harvesting it when the check's own ceiling is as likely, and the mend each reading asks for is the opposite of the other.

evidence:
Read 2026-09-14.

The words. The verdict store at /var/home/walton/.local/state/workstation-services/audit-verdicts.json holds, for check-reaches-a-path-through-the-index, a single refusal ending `died on SIGKILL apart, so it judged nothing — ` with nothing after the last dash, and `unrun` true. That text is built at check/modules/audit-serving/audit-serving.module.code.ts:169-172, where `endingOf` at util/run/modules/running/running.module.code.ts:414-416 answers `died on ${signal}` and `reasonSaid` carries whatever the child left on its error stream. An empty tail is what SIGKILL leaves, because the child never got to write.

Who can send it. One: `spawnedHere` at running.module.code.ts:357-392 spawns the watcher `watching` builds at :221-240 whenever the check states an audit processor ceiling, and that watcher writes `cgroup.kill`, which is SIGKILL to every process in the group. Two: `leftSwept` at :180-194 writes `cgroup.kill` to every `akasha-<pid>-<nanos>` group whose maker `stillMaking` reads as gone; `budgetAt` calls it at :208 on every spawn, and the reaper tick calls it at infrastructure/memory/reaping/modules/memory-reaper-tick/memory-reaper-tick.module.code.ts:39 every ten seconds. Three: anything outside. All three leave one sentence.

The reaper was not the sender on the round that raised the alarm. memory-reaper-kill.module.code.ts:16-63 signals SIGTERM and waits five seconds before SIGKILL, so what it takes usually dies on SIGTERM. `journalctl --user -u memory-reaper.service` since 2026-09-13 holds twenty kills, nineteen naming `tsc` and one naming `bun`, that one at 09:49:46 on 2026-09-14. The round that told the checks champion of five unmeasured checks ran from 09:08:02 to 09:58:03 that day at commit bb62ec74279e01aef046a60e092a2bde051a531b. One kill cannot account for five, and all five said SIGKILL rather than SIGTERM.

What the ceiling leaves. no-code-comments states `audit: { maxCpuSeconds: 15 }`. Its rows at check/code/pages/no-code-comments/no-code-comments.check-code.audit.logs.uncommitted.jsonl hold 32 audit runs. Twenty cost 5.2 to 6.5 processor seconds. The run at 2026-09-13T21:06:32Z cost 10.323 over 33.0 seconds of clock, and the one at 2026-09-14T14:06:58Z cost 8.984 over 27.5 seconds. Its last six runs, on a quiet machine, cost 8.0 to 9.9 with another 1.7 to 1.9 in a child, so 9.8 to 11.8 against the 15 it states. Half again as much passes the ceiling. No row exists for a round the check was killed in, because `recordCost` runs inside the child.

The pressure was real, and the audit felt it without being killed by it. Between 11:00:35 and 12:25:41 on 2026-09-14 the audit-running journal holds 44 lines of `landing-admission: audit waits for the 8 GB a landing starts on`, and in that same window the reaper killed a four-gigabyte `tsc` twelve times and nothing else. That round told the champion of three checks at commit 32d3e1f120a628e867a854b3207de843b313d538, kept as agent/messaging/message/pages/message-ed4c35303d8b.message.ts.

Why it is misread. Memory pressure is visible in a log and a processor ceiling is not, so a round of killed checks during pressure reads as the reaper harvesting them. The ceiling's other outcome reads as nothing alike: where `budgetAt` answers no group no watcher runs, the check finishes, and `ranOver` at check/modules/checking/checking.module.code.ts:138-151 refuses it in plain words for spending over its ceiling. One cause, two records, and neither names the other.
